analysis.evidence: נֹחַ is the first named subject, and אֶל הַתֵּבָה identifies the ark as the place Noah and his family entered. מִפְּנֵי מֵי הַמַּבּוּל gives their reason for entering.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: נֹחַ names the subject of וַיָּבֹא, “he entered.” His sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives enter the ark with him (אִתּוֹ) because of the floodwaters.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The suffix refers to Noah. The verse lists his sons, his wife, and the wives of his sons (וּנְשֵׁי בָנָיו), confirming the marital sense.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ plus feminine singular construct noun אִשְׁתּ־ with third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ.

analysis.evidence: נְשֵׁי is in construct with בָנָיו ‘his sons’. The phrase ‘the wives of his sons’ parallels וְאִשְׁתּוֹ ‘and his wife’ in the list of Noah’s family entering the ark.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ ‘and’ + נְשֵׁי, feminine plural construct noun.

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּבֹא … אֶל הַתֵּבָה, אֶל introduces the ark as the place Noah and his family entered to escape the floodwaters.

draft.change: Add the Hebrew noun תֵּבָה under its own consonants, תבה.
draft.definition: A vessel that holds and protects its occupants on water.
draft.evidence: Noah and his household enter the ark because of the floodwaters in Gen.7.7, and the rising waters lift it in Gen.7.17.

analysis.evidence: וַיָּבֹא … אֶל הַתֵּבָה says that Noah and his family went into the ark. מִפְּנֵי מֵי הַמַּבּוּל gives their reason for entering it: the floodwaters.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun.
analysis.sense: The vessel that carried Noah and his household on the floodwaters.

analysis.evidence: אֶל הַתֵּבָה gives the destination, “into the ark.” מִפְּנֵי מֵי הַמַּבּוּל gives the reason Noah and his family entered, “because of the floodwaters.”
analysis.morphology: Compound preposition formed from prefixed מִן and פְּנֵי, the plural construct of פָּנִים. The נ of מִן assimilates to פּ.

draft.change: Add Genesis 7:7 as evidence for the literal floodwater sense in the existing mayim article.
draft.definition: A body or flow of water, including the waters of a flood.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:7 uses מֵי הַמַּבּוּל, “the waters of the flood,” for the waters that prompted Noah and his family to enter the ark.

analysis.evidence: מֵי is the construct form of מַיִם. The following noun הַמַּבּוּל specifies which waters. Together, מִפְּנֵי מֵי הַמַּבּוּל means “because of the waters of the flood” and explains why Noah and his family entered the ark.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: a body or flow of water

draft.change: Revise the existing flood sense to define the inundation itself. Add the Genesis evidence and retain Psalm 29:10 as an example.
draft.definition: An inundation in which rising waters cover the land.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:7 calls the waters that drove Noah’s family into the ark “the waters of the flood.” Genesis 7:17 describes the flood as the waters rise and lift the ark.

analysis.evidence: In מֵי הַמַּבּוּל, “the waters of the flood,” מֵי is the construct form of מַיִם, and הַמַּבּוּל identifies the flood to which the waters belong. The whole phrase follows מִפְּנֵי and gives the reason Noah and his family entered the ark.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun. The article doubles the initial מ. No suffix.
